questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText: The simple epithelium characterized by a single thin layer of flattened cells with irregular boundaries, primarily involved in forming a diffusion boundary, is found in the:
options: A) Air sacs of lungs and walls of blood vessels
B) Tubular parts of nephrons in kidneys and ducts of salivary glands
C) Inner lining of the stomach and intestine
D) Moist surface of the buccal cavity and pharynx
questions.explanation: Simple squamous epithelium consists of a single thin layer of flattened cells with irregular boundaries. It is functionally specialized for forming a diffusion boundary and is characteristically located in the air sacs (alveoli) of lungs and the walls of blood vessels (endothelium). Tubular parts of nephrons possess cuboidal epithelium (Option B), stomach lining has columnar epithelium (Option C), and buccal cavity is lined by compound non-keratinized stratified epithelium (Option D).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText: The epithelium found in the proximal convoluted tubule (PCT) of the nephron in human kidneys, which possesses microvilli to increase the surface area for reabsorption, is:
options: A) Ciliated columnar epithelium
B) Simple cuboidal epithelium
C) Keratinized stratified squamous epithelium
D) Non-ciliated simple columnar epithelium
questions.explanation: Simple cuboidal epithelium consists of a single layer of cube-like cells commonly found in ducts of glands and tubular parts of nephrons. The epithelium of the proximal convoluted tubule (PCT) of the nephron characteristically possesses microvilli on its apical surface to facilitate extensive tubular reabsorption. Bronchioles have ciliated columnar/cuboidal cells (Option A), skin has stratified squamous epithelium (Option C), and the stomach lining has columnar cells (Option D).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText: Which of the following animal tissues lines the inner surface of hollow tubular organs such as the fallopian tubes and bronchioles to move particles or mucus in a specific direction?
options: A) Compound squamous epithelium
B) Brush-bordered cuboidal epithelium
C) Ciliated epithelium
D) Glandular columnar epithelium
questions.explanation: If columnar or cuboidal cells bear cilia on their free surface, they are termed ciliated epithelium. Their primary function is to move particles or mucus in a specific direction over the epithelial surface. They are characteristically found on the inner surface of hollow organs such as bronchioles and fallopian tubes (oviducts). Compound epithelium functions in protection against mechanical stress (Option A), brush-bordered cuboidal aids reabsorption in PCT (Option B), and glandular epithelium secretes chemicals (Option D).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText: In animal tissues, specialized intercellular junctions that facilitate rapid cytoplasmic communication between adjacent cells by allowing the passage of ions, small molecules, and sometimes macromolecules are known as:
options: A) Tight junctions
B) Adhering junctions
C) Desmosomes
D) Gap junctions
questions.explanation: Gap junctions facilitate rapid communication between adjacent cells by connecting the cytoplasm of adjoining cells, allowing swift transfer of ions, small molecules, and sometimes macromolecules. Tight junctions help stop substances from leaking across an epithelial sheet (Option A). Adhering junctions perform cementing to keep neighbouring cells together (Option B). Desmosomes are anchoring junctions providing mechanical stability (Option C).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText: Glandular epithelium is categorized into unicellular and multicellular glands based on cell organization. An example of isolated unicellular glandular cells in the human body is:
options: A) Salivary gland cells
B) Goblet cells of the alimentary canal
C) Sebaceous gland cells
D) Acinar cells of the pancreas
questions.explanation: Glandular epithelium consists of specialized epithelial cells that synthesize and secrete substances. They are classified into: (1) Unicellular glands, which consist of isolated glandular cells, such as goblet cells of the alimentary canal; and (2) Multicellular glands, consisting of clusters of cells, such as salivary glands (Option A), sebaceous glands (Option C), and pancreatic acinar cells (Option D).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText: Which of the following body surfaces is primarily lined by compound (stratified) epithelium to provide protection against chemical and mechanical stresses?
options: A) Moist lining of the buccal cavity and pharynx
B) Alveoli of the lungs and blood capillaries
C) Proximal and distal convoluted tubules of the nephron
D) Mucosal lining of the stomach and small intestine
questions.explanation: Compound epithelium consists of two or more cell layers and has a limited role in absorption and secretion; its primary function is to provide protection against chemical and mechanical stresses. It covers the dry surface of the skin, the moist surface of the buccal cavity, the pharynx, inner lining of ducts of salivary glands, and pancreatic ducts. Alveoli have simple squamous (Option B), nephrons have simple cuboidal (Option C), and stomach/intestine have simple columnar epithelium (Option D).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText: Areolar connective tissue, present beneath the skin, serves as a support framework for epithelium. Which of the following sets of cells is normally found distributed within its matrix?
options: A) Chondrocytes, osteocytes, and erythrocytes
B) Podocytes, mesangial cells, and lymphocytes
C) Adipocytes, thrombocytes, and Schwann cells
D) Fibroblasts, macrophages, and mast cells
questions.explanation: Areolar tissue is a type of loose connective tissue present beneath the skin. It contains fibers and cells loosely arranged in a semi-fluid ground substance. The resident cells include fibroblasts (cells that produce and secrete fibers), macrophages (phagocytic cells), and mast cells (which release histamine, serotonin, and heparin). Chondrocytes are in cartilage (Option A), podocytes are in Bowman's capsule (Option B), and Schwann cells myelinate peripheral nerves (Option C).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText: Tendons and ligaments are classic examples of dense connective tissue. What structural feature distinguishes dense regular connective tissue from dense irregular connective tissue?
options: A) Orientation of collagen fibers in parallel bundles in dense regular tissue
B) Absence of collagen fibers in dense regular connective tissue
C) Presence of a fluid matrix containing dissolved albumin and globulin
D) Complete lack of fibroblast cells between collagen bundles
questions.explanation: In dense regular connective tissue, the collagen fibers are oriented in parallel rows between many parallel bundles of fibers, providing high tensile strength in a single direction (e.g., tendons attaching skeletal muscles to bones, and ligaments attaching bone to bone). In dense irregular connective tissue, fibroblasts and many fibers (mostly collagen) are oriented haphazardly/irregularly to resist multi-directional forces (present in skin dermis). Both contain collagen and fibroblasts (rejecting Options B and D). Fluid matrix is characteristic of vascular tissue (Option C).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText: The specialized connective tissue whose intercellular matrix is solid, pliable, and resists compression, with cells (chondrocytes) enclosed in small cavities called lacunae, is:
options: A) Compact bone
B) Dense irregular dermis
C) Cartilage
D) Adipose tissue
questions.explanation: Cartilage has a solid and pliable intercellular matrix that resists compression. Chondrocytes (cartilage cells) are enclosed in small fluid-filled cavities called lacunae within the secreted matrix. Bone matrix is hard and non-pliable due to calcium phosphate salts and collagen fibers (Option A). Dermis consists of dense irregular tissue (Option B). Adipose tissue consists of fat-storing cells with minimal extracellular fibers (Option D).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText: Smooth muscle fibers differ significantly from skeletal muscle fibers in histological appearance and innervation. Smooth muscle fibers are characterized as being:
options: A) Cylindrical, syncytial (multinucleated), and voluntary
B) Branched, uninucleated, and striated with intercalated discs
C) Non-tapering, multinucleated, and under conscious control
D) Spindle-shaped (fusiform), unstriated, and involuntary
questions.explanation: Smooth muscle fibers taper at both ends (spindle-shaped / fusiform) and do not show striations (unstriated). Cell junctions hold them together, and they are bundled in a connective tissue sheath. They are involuntary and uninucleated, commonly found in the walls of visceral organs like blood vessels, stomach, and intestine. Option A describes skeletal muscle fibers, while Option B describes cardiac muscle fibers.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText: Cardiac muscle tissue is a contractile tissue present only in the heart. Communication junctions (intercalated discs) at some fusion points function to:
options: A) Allow the cells to contract as a coordinated unit by transmitting depolarization waves
B) Anchor cardiac muscle fibers directly to the thoracic rib cage
C) Prevent any ionic flow between adjacent cardiomyocytes to stop arrhythmia
D) Convert cardiac striated muscle fibers into non-striated smooth fibers
questions.explanation: Intercalated discs are specialized communication junctions located at transverse fusion points between adjacent cardiac muscle cells. They contain gap junctions and desmosomes that allow wave depolarization and ionic passage between adjacent cells, enabling the entire myocardium to contract as a single functional syncytium/unit. They do not anchor to ribs (Option B), they promote rather than prevent ionic flow (Option C), and cardiomyocytes remain striated (Option D).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText: In the neural system, which component makes up more than one-half the total volume of neural tissue in the human body, providing structural support and protection to neurons?
options: A) Dendrites
B) Neuroglial cells
C) Axon hillocks
D) Nodes of Ranvier
questions.explanation: Neuroglia (neuroglial cells) constitute the supportive, non-conducting component of the nervous system. According to NCERT, neuroglia make up more than one-half the volume of neural tissue in the human body. They protect and support the excitable neurons. Dendrites (Option A), axon hillocks (Option C), and nodes of Ranvier (Option D) are specialized structural components of individual neurons.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText: The exoskeleton of the common cockroach (Periplaneta americana) consists of hardened chitinous plates called sclerites. The dorsal plates and ventral plates are termed respectively as:
options: A) Pleurites and sternites
B) Sternites and tergites
C) Tergites and sternites
D) Tergites and pleurites
questions.explanation: In each segment of a cockroach, the exoskeleton consists of hardened chitinous plates called sclerites. Dorsally, these plates are known as tergites (or terga), and ventrally they are called sternites (or sterna). The lateral plates between them are called pleurites. Tergites and sternites are joined to each other by a thin, flexible articular membrane known as the arthrodial membrane.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText: The head of a cockroach is triangular in shape and lies at a right angle to the longitudinal body axis. This condition where the mouthparts are directed downwards is known as:
options: A) Prognathous
B) Opisthognathous
C) Epignathous
D) Hypognathous
questions.explanation: The head of Periplaneta americana is triangular and attached to the thorax via a short, flexible neck. It is positioned at a right angle ($90^\circ$) to the longitudinal body axis with the biting mouthparts directed downwards, a morphological condition termed hypognathous. In prognathous insects (Option A), the head is directed forward along the body axis.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText: In the thorax of Periplaneta americana, the forewings (tegmina) arise from which thoracic segment and what is their primary function?
options: A) Prothorax; generating aerodynamic lift during sustained flight
B) Metathorax; functioning as auditory balancing halteres
C) Mesothorax; generating thrust during high-speed flight
D) Mesothorax; protecting the delicate hindwings at rest
questions.explanation: Cockroaches bear two pairs of wings on the thorax. The first pair, the forewings or tegmina, arises from the mesothorax. Tegmina are opaque, dark, and leathery, and their primary function is protective—covering and shielding the membranous hindwings when at rest. They are not used in flight. The hindwings arise from the metathorax and are transparent, membranous, and used actively in flight (rejecting Options A, B, and C).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText: A key external morphological feature used to distinguish a male cockroach from a female cockroach is the presence of:
options: A) A pair of short, unjointed anal styles on the 9th sternite
B) A pair of jointed filamentous anal cerci on the 10th segment
C) Brood (genital) pouch formed by the 7th, 8th, and 9th sternites
D) Compound eyes consisting of ~2000 hexagonal ommatidia
questions.explanation: Male cockroaches bear a pair of short, thread-like, unjointed anal styles on the 9th sternite, which are completely absent in females. This serves as the definitive external diagnostic feature for sex determination. Anal cerci (Option B) are present on the 10th abdominal segment in both sexes. The brood or genital pouch formed by the 7th, 8th, and 9th sternites is present in females (Option C). Both sexes have compound eyes with ~2000 ommatidia (Option D).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText: In the alimentary canal of Periplaneta americana, the gizzard (proventriculus) is structurally specialized for grinding food particles by having:
options: A) A thick outer layer of longitudinal muscles and an inner lining of cilia
B) 100 to 150 yellow-colored hair-like filaments that secrete bile salts
C) A thick circular muscle layer and a thick inner cuticle forming six chitinous teeth
D) A glandular mucosa containing millions of oxyntic and peptic cells
questions.explanation: The gizzard (proventriculus) of the cockroach has an outer layer of thick circular muscles and a thick inner cuticular lining that forms six highly chitinous plates called 'teeth'. These teeth, along with fine bristles behind them, grind food particles into a fine powder. Hepatic caeca (6-8 blind tubules) secrete digestive juice, whereas 100-150 Malpighian tubules perform excretion (Option B). The cockroach lacks mammalian gastric oxyntic/peptic cells (Option D).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText: At the junction of the foregut and midgut in the digestive system of cockroach, a ring of 6 to 8 blind tubules is present, known as:
options: A) Hepatic (gastric) caeca, which secrete digestive juice
B) Malpighian tubules, which extract uric acid from haemolymph
C) Collaterial glands, which form the protective ootheca
D) Conglobate glands, which store spermatophores
questions.explanation: At the junction of the foregut (stomodaeum) and midgut (mesenteron), a ring of 6 to 8 blind finger-like tubules called hepatic or gastric caeca is present; these secrete digestive enzymes into the midgut. Malpighian tubules (Option B) are 100-150 yellow tubules located at the midgut-hindgut junction. Collaterial glands (Option C) are accessory reproductive glands in females, and the conglobate gland (Option D) is an accessory gland in males.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText: The primary excretory organs of Periplaneta americana are Malpighian tubules. Which of the following statements correctly describes their number, location, and nature of excretion?
options: A) 10 to 12 pairs in the thorax; ammonotelic excretion directly into trachea
B) 100 to 150 thin yellow filaments at the midgut-hindgut junction; uricotelic excretion
C) 6 to 8 tubules at the foregut-midgut junction; ureotelic excretion
D) A single pair of nephridial organs in the 10th abdominal segment; aminotelic
questions.explanation: Cockroaches possess 100 to 150 thin, yellow-colored filamentous Malpighian tubules situated at the junction of the midgut and hindgut. They absorb nitrogenous waste products (potassium urate) from the haemolymph, convert them into uric acid, and discharge it into the hindgut, making the cockroach uricotelic. Hepatic caeca are 6-8 in number at the foregut-midgut junction (Option C).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText: The circulatory system of the cockroach is open type with poorly developed vessels opening into the haemocoel. The tubular heart is situated along the mid-dorsal line and consists of how many chambers?
options: A) 4 chambers
B) 8 chambers
C) 10 chambers
D) 13 chambers
questions.explanation: The heart of Periplaneta americana is an elongated, pulsatile, muscular tube lying along the mid-dorsal line of the thorax and abdomen. It is differentiated into 13 funnel-shaped chambers (3 thoracic and 10 abdominal), each possessing lateral ostia with valves that permit the unidirectional entry of haemolymph from the pericardial sinus into the heart.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText: In the respiratory system of the cockroach, atmospheric air enters and exits the tracheal trunk through lateral openings called spiracles. How many pairs of spiracles are present on the body?
options: A) 12 pairs (3 thoracic pairs and 9 abdominal pairs)
B) 10 pairs (2 thoracic pairs and 8 abdominal pairs)
C) 8 pairs (all located exclusively on abdominal segments)
D) 13 pairs (corresponding to the 13 chambers of the heart)
questions.explanation: The respiratory system of the cockroach consists of a network of tracheae that open to the exterior through 10 pairs of small slits called spiracles situated on the lateral sides of the body. Of these, 2 pairs are situated on the thorax (one between pro- and mesothorax, one between meso- and metathorax) and 8 pairs are located on the first eight abdominal segments.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText: The type of embryonic and post-embryonic development observed in the cockroach (Periplaneta americana), involving progression through multiple nymphal instars, is termed:
options: A) Holometabolous (complete metamorphosis via larva and pupa)
B) Ametabolous (direct development without any nymphal stages)
C) Paurometabolous (gradual metamorphosis through about 13 nymphal moults)
D) Retrogressive metamorphosis (degenerative transformation)
questions.explanation: The development of Periplaneta americana is paurometabolous, meaning development is gradual through a series of nymphal stages. The nymph looks very much like the adult. The nymph grows by moulting about 13 times to reach the adult form. The next-to-last nymphal stage has wing pads, but only the adult cockroach has functional wings. Holometabolous insects (e.g., butterflies, beetles) have distinct egg, larva, pupa, and adult stages (Option A).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding connective tissues:
Statement I: In areolar connective tissue, fibroblasts, macrophages, and mast cells are loosely distributed within a semi-fluid ground substance.
Statement II: In dense regular connective tissue, tendons attach one bone to another bone, whereas ligaments connect skeletal muscles to bones.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
C) Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect
D) Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze Statement I. Areolar tissue is indeed a loose connective tissue located beneath the skin where fibers and cells (fibroblasts, macrophages, and mast cells) are loosely arranged in a semi-fluid ground substance. Hence, Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Analyze Statement II. Tendons attach skeletal muscles to bones (dense regular connective tissue), while ligaments attach one bone to another bone. Statement II reverses these anatomical definitions and is therefore incorrect.
Step 3: Conclusion. Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect (Option C).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Ciliated epithelium lines the luminal surface of hollow internal organs such as fallopian tubes and bronchioles.
Reason (R): The coordinated, rhythmic beating of cilia propels mucus, trapped foreign particles, or ovulated ova in a specific unidirectional path over the epithelial surface.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
C) Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false
D) Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Assess Assertion (A). Ciliated columnar or cuboidal epithelium possesses motile hair-like cilia on its apical free surface and characteristically lines the inner surface of bronchioles and fallopian tubes. Thus, (A) is true.
Step 2: Assess Reason (R). The functional purpose of these cilia is to generate continuous rhythmic forward strokes that move mucus and ova in a specific direction. Thus, (R) is true.
Step 3: Evaluate explanation link. The presence of cilia in these specific hollow tubular organs is biologically necessitated by the requirement for unidirectional transport. Hence, Reason (R) correctly explains Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding skeletal connective tissues:
Statement I: Cartilage is characterized by an entirely rigid, calcified, and non-pliable matrix that completely prevents any mechanical flexibility.
Statement II: In adult vertebrates, all embryonic cartilaginous skeletal structures are permanently retained without undergoing endochondral ossification into bone.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
C) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
D) Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. According to NCERT, the intercellular material of cartilage is solid and pliable, and resists compression, whereas bone has a hard and non-pliable ground substance rich in calcium salts and collagen fibers. Thus, Statement I is completely false.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. Most of the cartilages in vertebrate embryos are replaced by bones in adults; only some persist (e.g., tip of nose, outer ear joints, between adjacent bones of the vertebral column). Hence, Statement II is also false.
Step 3: Conclusion. Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect (Option B).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Compound (stratified) epithelium plays an extensive, primary role in active nutrient absorption and biochemical secretion across the human intestinal lumen.
Reason (R): Compound epithelium consists of two or more cell layers whose primary evolutionary role is to provide mechanical and chemical protection rather than secretion or absorption.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
C) Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false
D) Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze Assertion (A). Active absorption and secretion in the digestive tract are carried out by simple columnar epithelium (equipped with microvilli and goblet cells), not compound epithelium. Compound epithelium has a limited role in secretion and absorption. Thus, (A) is false.
Step 2: Analyze Reason (R). Being multi-layered, compound epithelium provides barrier protection against mechanical abrasions, chemical damage, and desiccation (e.g., in skin epidermis, buccal cavity, and pharynx). Thus, (R) is true.
Step 3: Conclusion. Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true (Option D).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding cell junctions in animal tissues:
Statement I: Tight junctions facilitate rapid cytoplasmic continuity and direct passage of ions and second messengers between adjacent epithelial cells.
Statement II: Adhering junctions perform cementing to keep neighbouring cells together and maintain tissue structural integrity.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
B) Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct
C) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
D) Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze Statement I. Tight junctions function to stop substances from leaking across a tissue layer by sealing plasma membranes of adjacent cells together. Rapid transfer of ions, small molecules, and second messengers is the characteristic function of gap junctions, not tight junctions. Hence, Statement I is incorrect.
Step 2: Analyze Statement II. Adhering junctions (zonula adherens and desmosomes) serve to cement neighbouring cells together through cadherins and intermediate filaments, maintaining structural coherence. Hence, Statement II is correct.
Step 3: Conclusion. Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct (Option B).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Both skeletal muscle fibers and cardiac muscle fibers display microscopic alternating dark (A) and light (I) bands (striations).
Reason (R): Both skeletal and cardiac muscle tissues are syncytial (multinucleated) and contract exclusively under voluntary conscious somatic innervation.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
C) Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false
D) Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Assertion (A). Skeletal muscle fibers and cardiac muscle cells both have organized sarcomerestructure with regular arrangements of actin and myosin filaments, giving them a striated appearance under light microscopy. Thus, (A) is true.
Step 2: Evaluate Reason (R). Skeletal muscle fibers are multinucleated (syncytial) and voluntary. However, cardiac muscle cells are uninucleated, branched, involuntary (controlled by autonomic innervation and intrinsic nodal rhythmicity), and interconnected by intercalated discs. Thus, (R) is false.
Step 3: Conclusion. Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false (Option C).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding neural tissue:
Statement I: Neurons are excitable cells that generate and propagate electrochemical action potentials upon stimulation.
Statement II: Neuroglia constitute more than $50\%$ of the total volume of neural tissue in the human body, providing essential physical and physiological protection to neurons.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
C) Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect
D) Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. Neurons are specialized, excitable cells capable of sensing stimuli, generating depolarization waves, and conducting electric impulses (action potentials) along their axons. Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. According to NCERT Class 11, neuroglia make up more than one-half (over $50\%$) of the total volume of neural tissue in the human body. They insulate, support, protect, and nourish neurons. Statement II is correct.
Step 3: Conclusion. Both Statement I and Statement II are correct (Option A).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): The compound eyes of Periplaneta americana produce a mosaic vision characterized by high sensitivity but low resolution, which is highly advantageous for nocturnal navigation.
Reason (R): In Periplaneta americana, the paired, long, filamentous antennae bear sensory receptors that continuously monitor environmental tactile and chemical stimuli.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
C) Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false
D) Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze Assertion (A). Cockroach vision is termed mosaic vision because each compound eye contains about $2000$ hexagonal ommatidia, each capturing a separate segment of the visual field. This confers high sensitivity to dim light but low optical resolution, typical for nocturnal insects. Thus, (A) is true.
Step 2: Analyze Reason (R). Antennae in cockroaches are indeed sensory appendages containing tactile, olfactory, and thermal receptors that sample the environment. Thus, (R) is true.
Step 3: Evaluate explanation relationship. While both statements are scientifically true facts from NCERT, the sensory function of the antennae does not explain why the ommatidia in compound eyes produce mosaic vision (which is due to optical isolation of ommatidial units). Therefore, (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A) (Option B).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding the head and mouthparts of Periplaneta americana:
Statement I: The head of Periplaneta americana is formed by the embryonic fusion of only three segments and is rigidly immovable due to the complete absence of a neck region.
Statement II: The mouthparts consist of a labrum (upper lip), a pair of mandibles with grinding and incising surfaces, a pair of maxillae, a labium (lower lip), and a median hypopharynx acting as a tongue.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
C) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
D) Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Examine Statement I. The head capsule of the cockroach is formed by the embryonic fusion of six segments (not three) and exhibits great flexibility and mobility in all directions due to a flexible neck (cervix). Hence, Statement I is incorrect.
Step 2: Examine Statement II. The mouthparts are of the biting and chewing type, comprising an anterior labrum (upper lip), a pair of dentate mandibles, a pair of first maxillae, a posterior labium (lower lip), and a median chitinous lobe called the hypopharynx (lingua/tongue). Hence, Statement II is completely correct.
Step 3: Conclusion. Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct (Option D).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): In Periplaneta americana, respiratory gases ($O_2$ and $CO_2$) are transported directly to and from body cells via tracheoles without depending on haemolymph for transport.
Reason (R): The haemolymph of cockroach is devoid of respiratory pigments such as haemoglobin or haemocyanin, consisting of colourless plasma and haemocytes.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
C) Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false
D) Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Verify Assertion (A). Cockroaches possess an extensive tracheal network where air enters through 10 pairs of spiracles, travels through tracheal trunks, and diffuses directly across fluid-filled tracheolar endings into tissue cells without circulatory gas delivery. Thus, (A) is true.
Step 2: Verify Reason (R). Cockroach haemolymph does not contain any oxygen-carrying respiratory pigments (like haemoglobin); hence, it cannot transport respiratory gases and carries only nutrients and metabolic wastes. Thus, (R) is true.
Step 3: Evaluate causal link. Because the haemolymph cannot bind and transport $O_2$, the tracheal system must deliver air directly to cells. Therefore, (R) is the precise physiological explanation of (A) (Option A).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding the digestive tract of Periplaneta americana:
Statement I: The proventriculus (gizzard) possesses a thick outer layer of circular muscles and an inner cuticular lining that forms six highly chitinous teeth to grind solid food.
Statement II: Hepatic caeca are a ring of $100\text{--}150$ yellow filamentous tubules located at the midgut-hindgut junction whose sole function is the reabsorption of water.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
C) Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect
D) Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Assess Statement I. The gizzard (proventriculus) has an outer layer of thick circular muscles and a thick inner cuticular layer that forms six teeth; it functions as a muscular masticatory chamber. Thus, Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Assess Statement II. Hepatic (gastric) caeca are a ring of $6\text{--}8$ blind tubules located at the junction of foregut and midgut that secrete digestive juices. The $100\text{--}150$ yellow filamentous tubules located at the midgut-hindgut junction are Malpighian tubules, which perform excretion. Thus, Statement II is incorrect.
Step 3: Conclusion. Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect (Option C).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Periplaneta americana is an uricotelic insect adapted to minimize water loss by excreting nitrogenous waste as semi-solid uric acid.
Reason (R): Malpighian tubules absorb soluble potassium urate from the haemolymph, convert it to insoluble uric acid within their glandular-ciliated epithelium, and pass it into the hindgut.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false
B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
C) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false
D) Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Examine Assertion (A). Cockroaches live in terrestrial environments where water conservation is critical. They excrete nitrogenous waste primarily as uric acid crystals in faeces, making them uricotelic. Thus, (A) is true.
Step 2: Examine Reason (R). Malpighian tubules, lined with glandular and ciliated cells, absorb potassium urate from the surrounding haemolymph. Inside the tubule, potassium bicarbonate is reabsorbed, precipitating uric acid, which is directed into the ileum and rectum where water is reclaimed before excretion. Thus, (R) is true.
Step 3: Evaluate explanation relationship. The active conversion and excretion of uric acid by Malpighian tubules directly explains why the cockroach is uricotelic and conserves water. Hence, Reason (R) correctly explains Assertion (A) (Option B).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding the male reproductive anatomy of Periplaneta americana:
Statement I: A pair of multi-lobed testes lies dorso-laterally in the $4^{\text{th}}\text{--}6^{\text{th}}$ abdominal segments.
Statement II: The mushroom-shaped gland (utricular gland) is an accessory reproductive gland present in the $6^{\text{th}}\text{--}7^{\text{th}}$ abdominal segments whose secretions help form the walls of spermatophores.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
C) Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect
D) Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Check Statement I. In male cockroaches, the paired testes are located laterally in the $4^{\text{th}}$, $5^{\text{th}}$, and $6^{\text{th}}$ abdominal segments. Sperms pass from testes through thin vasa deferentia into the ejaculatory duct. Hence, Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Check Statement II. The mushroom gland (consisting of long peripheral utriculi majores and short central utriculi breviores) is located in the $6^{\text{th}}\text{--}7^{\text{th}}$ abdominal segments and acts as an accessory reproductive gland, contributing secretions to package sperms into spermatophores. Hence, Statement II is correct.
Step 3: Conclusion. Both Statement I and Statement II are correct (Option A).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): In female Periplaneta americana, each ovary is composed of a group of eight ovarian tubules (ovarioles) containing a linear succession of developing ova.
Reason (R): A pair of spermathecae is located in the $2^{\text{nd}}$ abdominal segment and opens directly into the midgut to provide nourishment to stored sperms.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
C) Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false
D) Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze Assertion (A). Female cockroaches have two large ovaries located laterally in the $2^{\text{nd}}\text{--}6^{\text{th}}$ abdominal segments. Each ovary is formed of 8 ovarioles containing chains of developing follicles/oocytes. Thus, (A) is true.
Step 2: Analyze Reason (R). The spermatheca is a single pair of unequal sac-like structures located in the $6^{\text{th}}$ abdominal segment (not $2^{\text{nd}}$) that opens into the dorsal wall of the genital chamber, not into the midgut. Thus, (R) is false.
Step 3: Conclusion. Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false (Option C).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding the nervous system of Periplaneta americana:
Statement I: The nervous system consists of segmentally arranged paired ganglia joined by longitudinal connectives along the ventral midline.
Statement II: There are three ganglia situated in the thorax and six ganglia situated in the abdomen, while the brain is represented by the supra-oesophageal ganglion supplying the antennae and compound eyes.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
C) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
D) Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. The nervous system of the cockroach is ventral, solid, and consists of a double ventral nerve cord with segmentally arranged ganglia connected by paired inter-ganglionic connectives. Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. There are a total of 9 ganglia on the ventral cord: 3 thoracic (prothoracic, mesothoracic, metathoracic) and 6 abdominal ganglia. The supra-oesophageal ganglion lies above the oesophagus in the head, functioning as the brain and innervating the antennae and compound eyes. Statement II is correct.
Step 3: Conclusion. Both Statement I and Statement II are correct (Option B).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding ootheca formation and nymphal development in Periplaneta americana:
Statement I: A female cockroach produces only a single ootheca in its entire adult life, which encloses exactly $4\text{--}6$ fertilized eggs.
Statement II: An ootheca is a dark reddish to blackish-brown capsule about $8\text{ mm}$ long, and nymphs undergo roughly $13$ moults before attaining adulthood with mature wings.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
B) Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect
C) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
D) Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. On average, female cockroaches produce $9\text{--}10$ oothecae throughout their adult life, and each ootheca encapsulates $14\text{--}16$ fertilized eggs arranged in two parallel rows. Statement I is false.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. The ootheca is a dark reddish to blackish-brown chitinous capsule about $8\text{ mm}$ ($3/8\text{ inch}$) long, secreted by collaterial glands. Development is paurometabolous, and the nymph moults about 13 times to reach adult form. Statement II is true.
Step 3: Conclusion. Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct (Option D).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): In the Indian bullfrog (Rana tigrina), cutaneous respiration operates continuously whether the animal is submerged in water or undergoing hibernation and aestivation on land.
Reason (R): Frog skin is kept persistently moist by mucous gland secretions and is richly vascularized with sub-epithelial blood capillaries, allowing dissolved oxygen to diffuse directly into blood.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
C) Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false
D) Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Assess Assertion (A). In Rana tigrina, cutaneous respiration serves as the sole respiratory mode during hibernation (winter sleep) and aestivation (summer sleep), and when submerged in water. Thus, (A) is true.
Step 2: Assess Reason (R). For gas exchange across skin, the surface must be moist and thin. Frogs have highly vascularized integument coated with mucus that dissolves atmospheric or aquatic $O_2$ to diffuse into blood. Thus, (R) is true.
Step 3: Evaluate causal link. The moist, highly vascularized skin provides the physical substrate enabling continuous cutaneous respiration. Hence, Reason (R) correctly explains Assertion (A) (Option A).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding the internal organ systems of the frog (Rana tigrina):
Statement I: The alimentary canal of the frog is comparatively short because frogs are carnivorous, which necessitates a shorter intestine than herbivores.
Statement II: The frog heart is a three-chambered muscular organ consisting of two atria and a single ventricle, enclosed by a protective double-layered pericardium.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
B) Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct
C) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
D) Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Check Statement I. As noted in NCERT Class 11, the alimentary canal of the frog is short because frogs are carnivorous, and hence the length of the intestine is reduced compared to herbivores that require longer guts for cellulose digestion. Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Check Statement II. The heart of the frog is a muscular organ located in the upper body cavity, consisting of three chambers: two thin-walled atria (right and left) and a single thick-walled muscular ventricle. It is covered by a double-layered membrane called the pericardium. Statement II is correct.
Step 3: Conclusion. Both Statement I and Statement II are correct (Option C).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): In male frogs (Rana tigrina), the ureters are functionally designated as urogenital ducts because they convey both urine and spermatozoa to the cloaca.
Reason (R): $10\text{--}12$ vasa efferentia emerging from the testes enter the kidneys and open into Bidder's canal, which communicates directly with the ureters.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false
B) Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false
C) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
D) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze Assertion (A). In male frogs, the ureters conduct both excretory waste (urine from kidneys) and male gametes (sperms from testes) into the cloaca, hence they are termed urogenital ducts. In female frogs, ureters and oviducts open separately. Thus, (A) is true.
Step 2: Analyze Reason (R). Vasa efferentia (10 to 12 in number) arise from the testes, penetrate the medial border of the kidneys, and empty into a specialized longitudinal canal called Bidder's canal, which connects to the ureter. Thus, (R) is true.
Step 3: Evaluate explanation. Because the sperm pathway converges directly into the renal duct system via Bidder's canal, the ureter inevitably carries both urine and sperm, explaining the designation 'urogenital duct'. Thus, Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A) (Option D).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText:
Match List I with List II regarding types of epithelial tissues and their characteristic anatomical locations:
List I (Epithelial Type)
A. Simple squamous epithelium
B. Simple cuboidal epithelium with microvilli
C. Ciliated columnar epithelium
D. Compound (stratified) epithelium
List II (Characteristic Location)
I. Inner lining of fallopian tubes and bronchioles
II. Proximal convoluted tubule (PCT) of nephron
III. Alveolar air sacs of lungs and vascular endothelium
IV. Moist surface of buccal cavity and pharynx
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
B) A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV
C) A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV
D) A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Match A. Simple squamous epithelium forms a single thin layer of flattened cells with irregular margins, functioning as a diffusion boundary in pulmonary alveoli and capillary walls (endothelium). Thus, A matches with III.
Step 2: Match B. Simple cuboidal cells with an apical brush border of microvilli are characteristically found in the PCT of the nephron to maximize solute and water reabsorption. Thus, B matches with II.
Step 3: Match C and D. Ciliated epithelium lines hollow internal tubes like fallopian tubes and bronchioles to move mucus/ova unidirectionally (C matches with I). Compound epithelium is multi-layered and covers the moist surfaces subjected to mechanical friction like the buccal cavity and pharynx (D matches with IV). Hence, Option B (A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV) is correct.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements regarding animal cell junctions and tissue histology:
(i) Tight junctions help stop substances from leaking across an epithelial tissue sheet.
(ii) Adhering junctions perform cementing to keep neighbouring cells mechanically joined together.
(iii) Gap junctions facilitate rapid cytoplasmic communication between adjacent cells by permitting the transit of ions, small molecules, and sometimes macromolecules.
(iv) Gap junctions are completely absent in mammalian cardiac muscle tissue and smooth muscle tissue.
(v) Epithelial tissues are highly vascularized with dense arterial networks running directly between individual epithelial cells.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
options: A) (i), (ii), and (iv) only
B) (ii), (iii), (iv), and (v) only
C) (i), (ii), and (iii) only
D) (i), (iii), and (v) only
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate statements (i), (ii), and (iii). Statements (i), (ii), and (iii) are verbatim correct statements from NCERT regarding the three specialized cell junctions (tight junctions prevent leakages, adhering junctions cement cells, and gap junctions connect cytoplasm for rapid ionic/molecular communication).
Step 2: Evaluate statements (iv) and (v). Statement (iv) is false because gap junctions are abundant in cardiac muscle intercalated discs and in unitary smooth muscle, allowing electrical syncytial contraction. Statement (v) is false because epithelial tissues are avascular; they receive oxygen and nutrients by diffusion from underlying vascularized connective tissue across a basement membrane.
Step 3: Conclusion. Only statements (i), (ii), and (iii) are correct (Option C).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText:
Match List I with List II regarding connective tissues, their cellular organization, and their functions:
List I (Tissue / Structure)
A. Areolar tissue
B. Adipose tissue
C. Tendon
D. Cartilage
List II (Structural Feature / Cellular Composition)
I. Fibroblasts, macrophages, and mast cells loosely arranged in a semi-fluid ground substance beneath skin
II. Specialized loose connective tissue whose cells store fats in droplets beneath the skin
III. Dense regular connective tissue in which parallel bundles of collagen fibers attach skeletal muscle to bone
IV. Solid and pliable matrix resisting compression, containing chondrocytes enclosed in small lacunae
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
B) A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III
C) A-I, B-III, C-II, D-IV
D) A-IV, B-II, C-III, D-I
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Match A. Areolar tissue is a loose connective tissue serving as a supporting framework for epithelium beneath the skin; it contains fibroblasts, macrophages, and mast cells loosely suspended in a ground substance. Thus, A matches with I.
Step 2: Match B. Adipose tissue contains adipocytes optimized for fat storage under the skin to act as an energy depot and thermal insulator. Thus, B matches with II.
Step 3: Match C. Tendons consist of dense regular connective tissue with parallel rows of collagen fibers attaching muscles to bones. Thus, C matches with III.
Step 4: Match D. Cartilage matrix is solid and pliable (resisting compression) due to chondroitin salts, housing chondrocytes inside lacunae. Thus, D matches with IV. Hence, Option A (A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV) is correct.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements regarding the structural and functional classification of muscular tissues in vertebrates:
(i) Skeletal muscle fibers are striated, cylindrical, syncytial (multinucleated), and under voluntary control.
(ii) Smooth muscle fibers are non-striated, spindle-shaped (fusiform), uninucleated, and under involuntary autonomic control.
(iii) Cardiac muscle fibers are striated, branched, uninucleated, and joined together by intercalated discs.
(iv) Skeletal muscles are involuntary and are situated within the muscular walls of internal hollow visceral organs.
(v) The communication junctions (gap junctions) at intercalated discs of cardiac muscle allow cardiomyocytes to contract synchronously as a functional unit.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
options: A) (i), (ii), and (iv) only
B) (ii), (iv), and (v) only
C) (i), (iii), and (iv) only
D) (i), (ii), (iii), and (v) only
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate statements (i), (ii), and (iii). Skeletal muscle fibers are striated, multinucleated, unbranched, and voluntary (i is true). Smooth muscle fibers are spindle-shaped, unstriated, uninucleated, and involuntary (ii is true). Cardiac muscle fibers are branched, striated, uninucleated, and possess intercalated discs (iii is true).
Step 2: Evaluate statement (iv). Statement (iv) is completely false because visceral organs (blood vessels, stomach, intestine) contain involuntary smooth muscle, not voluntary skeletal muscle.
Step 3: Evaluate statement (v). Intercalated discs contain gap junctions that allow wave depolarization to spread rapidly across adjacent myocytes, coordinating synchronous contraction (v is true).
Step 4: Conclusion. Statements (i), (ii), (iii), and (v) are correct (Option D).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText:
Match List I with List II regarding the exoskeleton and external segmentation of Periplaneta americana:
List I (Anatomical Region / Sclerite)
A. Tergites
B. Sternites
C. Pleurites
D. Arthrodial membrane
List II (Morphological Description)
I. Thin, flexible articular membrane connecting adjacent sclerites to permit movement
II. Hardened chitinous plates covering the dorsal surface of each body segment
III. Hardened chitinous plates covering the ventral surface of each body segment
IV. Lateral chitinous plates located between the dorsal and ventral sclerites
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II
B) A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I
C) A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I
D) A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Match A and B. The body of the cockroach is segmented and covered by a brown chitinous exoskeleton. In each segment, the exoskeleton has hardened plates called sclerites. The dorsal sclerites are called tergites (A matches with II). The ventral sclerites are called sternites (B matches with III).
Step 2: Match C. The lateral sclerites on either side connecting terga and sterna are called pleurites (C matches with IV).
Step 3: Match D. All sclerites are joined to one another by a thin, flexible, articular membrane called the arthrodial membrane, which allows locomotion and respiratory expansion/contraction (D matches with I).
Step 4: Conclusion. Option B (A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I) is correct.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText:
Read the following statements regarding the head capsule and sensory receptors of Periplaneta americana:
(i) The head is triangular, formed by the embryonic fusion of six segments, and lies hypognathously with biting and chewing mouthparts.
(ii) Each compound eye consists of approximately $2000$ hexagonal ommatidia providing mosaic vision with high sensitivity and low resolution.
(iii) The long antennae arise from membranous sockets in front of the eyes and bear tactile and olfactory receptors.
(iv) Male cockroaches possess a pair of jointed, sensory anal styles attached to the $10^{\text{th}}$ abdominal tergite.
(v) Anal cerci are paired, jointed filamentous structures present on the $10^{\text{th}}$ abdominal segment in both sexes that detect ground and air vibrations.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
options: A) (i), (ii), and (iv) only
B) (ii), (iii), and (iv) only
C) (i), (ii), (iii), and (v) only
D) (i), (iv), and (v) only
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Check statements (i), (ii), and (iii). Statement (i) correctly states the 6-segment fusion and hypognathous posture. Statement (ii) accurately describes compound eyes with ~2000 ommatidia and mosaic nocturnal vision. Statement (iii) correctly describes antennal socket location and sensory reception.
Step 2: Check statement (iv). Statement (iv) is incorrect on two counts: anal styles are unjointed (not jointed) and arise from the $9^{\text{th}}$ sternite (not $10^{\text{th}}$ tergite).
Step 3: Check statement (v). Anal cerci are indeed paired, jointed structures present on the $10^{\text{th}}$ segment in both males and females, functioning as mechanoreceptors sensitive to sound and vibrations. Thus, (v) is correct.
Step 4: Conclusion. Statements (i), (ii), (iii), and (v) are correct (Option C).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText:
Match List I with List II regarding the alimentary canal of Periplaneta americana and the functional specialization of each part:
List I (Digestive Organ / Structure)
A. Crop
B. Gizzard (Proventriculus)
C. Hepatic (Gastric) caeca
D. Rectal papillae
List II (Functional Specialization)
I. Broad pyriform sac used for temporary storage of ingested food
II. Heavily muscularized organ with six chitinous teeth for grinding food
III. Ring of $6\text{--}8$ blind tubules at the foregut-midgut junction that secrete digestive enzymes
IV. Six internal cuticular pads in the rectal wall that actively reabsorb water and electrolytes
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
B) A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III
C) A-I, B-III, C-II, D-IV
D) A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Match A. The pharynx opens into a narrow oesophagus which leads into a large thin-walled distensible sac called the crop, used for storing food. Thus, A matches with I.
Step 2: Match B. The gizzard (proventriculus) has an outer layer of thick circular muscles and thick inner cuticle that forms six sharp chitinous teeth used for crushing food. Thus, B matches with II.
Step 3: Match C. At the junction of foregut and midgut, 6 to 8 blind tubules called hepatic or gastric caeca secrete digestive juice. Thus, C matches with III.
Step 4: Match D. The rectum opens out through the anus; its inner lining has 6 longitudinal rectal folds or papillae that absorb water and inorganic salts from faecal matter to prevent desiccation. Thus, D matches with IV. Hence, Option A is correct.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements regarding the circulatory and respiratory systems of Periplaneta americana:
(i) The circulatory system is of open type, and the tubular heart is differentiated into $13$ funnel-shaped chambers lying mid-dorsally.
(ii) Haemolymph enters each heart chamber from the pericardial sinus through lateral valve-guarded ostia.
(iii) Cockroach haemolymph is rich in copper-containing haemocyanin that facilitates oxygen binding and transport. 
(iv) The tracheal system opens to the outside through $10$ pairs of spiracles, of which $2$ pairs are thoracic and $8$ pairs are abdominal.
(v) Branching tracheoles penetrate into tissues, where exchange of respiratory gases occurs directly by diffusion without blood participation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
options: A) (i), (ii), and (iii) only
B) (ii), (iii), and (iv) only
C) (i), (iii), (iv), and (v) only
D) (i), (ii), (iv), and (v) only
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate statements (i) and (ii). Periplaneta has an open circulatory system with a 13-chambered dorsal tubular heart. Blood enters each chamber via lateral ostia during diastole and is pumped anteriorly into the cephalic aorta (statements i and ii are correct).
Step 2: Evaluate statement (iii). Statement (iii) is completely false because insect haemolymph does not contain any respiratory pigment (neither haemoglobin nor haemocyanin); it is colourless plasma with haemocytes and plays zero role in gas transport.
Step 3: Evaluate statements (iv) and (v). The respiratory system comprises 10 pairs of spiracles (2 thoracic, 8 abdominal) leading into tracheal trunks and branching tracheoles that supply $O_2$ directly to cell membranes by diffusion (statements iv and v are correct).
Step 4: Conclusion. Statements (i), (ii), (iv), and (v) are correct (Option D).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText:
Match List I with List II regarding reproductive organs and accessory structures in Periplaneta americana:
List I (Reproductive Structure)
A. Mushroom-shaped gland
B. Spermatheca
C. Collaterial glands
D. Phallic (Conglobate) gland
List II (Anatomical Details & Functions)
I. Paired sac-like structure in the $6^{\text{th}}$ abdominal segment of female opening into genital chamber to store sperms
II. Male accessory reproductive gland in the $6^{\text{th}}\text{--}7^{\text{th}}$ abdominal segments consisting of utriculi majores and breviores
III. Club-shaped male accessory gland lying ventral to ejaculatory duct whose secretion forms outer layer of spermatophore
IV. Paired branched female accessory glands whose secretions form the proteinaceous capsule of the ootheca
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
B) A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III
C) A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III
D) A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Match A. The mushroom-shaped gland (utricular gland) is an accessory gland in male cockroaches present in the 6th-7th abdominal segments (A matches with II).
Step 2: Match B. A pair of spermathecae is situated in the 6th abdominal segment of the female cockroach, opening into the dorsal wall of the genital pouch to store transferred spermatozoa (B matches with I).
Step 3: Match C. Collaterial glands are paired asymmetric branching glands located behind ovaries in females that secrete the milky fluid hardening into the oothecal shell (C matches with IV).
Step 4: Match D. The phallic (conglobate) gland is a large flat club-shaped accessory gland present in male cockroaches ventral to the nerve cord, contributing secretions to the outermost envelope of the spermatophore (D matches with III). Hence, Option B (A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III) is correct.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText:
Read the following statements regarding excretory physiology and organs in Periplaneta americana:
(i) Malpighian tubules are $100\text{--}150$ thin, yellow, blind filamentous structures situated at the junction of the midgut and hindgut.
(ii) Each Malpighian tubule is lined by glandular and ciliated epithelial cells that absorb soluble potassium urate from the surrounding haemolymph.
(iii) Inside the tubules, potassium urate is converted into insoluble uric acid, which is emptied into the hindgut and eliminated with faeces.
(iv) In addition to Malpighian tubules, the fat body, nephrocytes, and urecose glands also participate in excretory processes.
(v) Cockroaches are ammonotelic insects and lose copious amounts of body water to eliminate nitrogenous wastes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
options: A) (i), (ii), and (v) only
B) (ii), (iii), and (v) only
C) (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv) only
D) (i), (iv), and (v) only
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Verify statements (i), (ii), and (iii). Malpighian tubules are 100-150 yellow tubules located at the midgut-hindgut junction, lined by glandular and ciliated cells. They extract potassium urate from haemolymph, convert it to uric acid, and release it into the hindgut (statements i, ii, and iii are fully correct).
Step 2: Verify statement (iv). According to NCERT, in addition to Malpighian tubules, the fat body (containing urate cells), nephrocytes, and urecose glands (in male mushroom gland) also aid in excretion (statement iv is correct).
Step 3: Verify statement (v). Statement (v) is false because cockroaches are strictly uricotelic (not ammonotelic) and excrete dry crystalline uric acid to conserve water.
Step 4: Conclusion. Statements (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv) are correct (Option C).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText:
Match List I with List II regarding the cardiovascular, urogenital, and digestive anatomy of the frog (Rana tigrina):
List I (Anatomical Structure of Frog)
A. Bidder's canal
B. Sinus venosus
C. Conus arteriosus
D. Cloaca
List II (Morphological & Functional Description)
I. Muscular outflow tract arising from the single ventricle that distributes blood to the systemic, pulmo-cutaneous, and carotid arches
II. Specialized longitudinal canal in male frog kidney that connects vasa efferentia to the urogenital duct
III. Triangular venous chamber on the dorsal surface of the heart that collects systemic deoxygenated blood and empties into the right atrium
IV. Common terminal chamber into which the rectum, urinary bladder, and reproductive ducts discharge their contents
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
B) A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV
C) A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV
D) A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Match A. In male frogs, vasa efferentia (10-12 in number) enter the kidneys and open into Bidder's canal, which communicates with the ureter (urogenital duct). Thus, A matches with II.
Step 2: Match B. The sinus venosus is a triangular accessory chamber attached dorsally to the heart; it receives blood from three major caval veins (two precavals and one postcaval) and opens into the right atrium. Thus, B matches with III.
Step 3: Match C. The conus (truncus) arteriosus is a muscular arterial cone arising from the ventral base of the ventricle that bifurcates into branches leading to aortic arches. Thus, C matches with I.
Step 4: Match D. The cloaca is the small median chamber receiving digestive waste from the rectum, urine from the bladder/ureters, and gametes from gonoducts before exiting through the cloacal aperture. Thus, D matches with IV. Hence, Option B (A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV) is correct.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements regarding the morphological, physiological, and anatomical features of Rana tigrina:
(i) Frogs are poikilotherms (cold-blooded) and show camouflage (protective colouration) to hide from enemies, as well as winter sleep (hibernation) and summer sleep (aestivation).
(ii) Male frogs are distinguished externally from females by the presence of vocal sacs on either side of the throat and a copulatory (nuptial) pad on the first digit of the forelimbs.
(iii) Cutaneous respiration provides oxygen in aquatic environments and during dormancy, while pulmonary and buccopharyngeal respiration function primarily on land.
(iv) Vascular connections in frogs include both a hepatic portal system (connecting gut to liver) and a renal portal system (connecting posterior body parts to kidneys).
(v) Frogs possess an open circulatory system with a two-chambered heart that lacks any cardiac sinus structures.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
options: A) (i), (ii), and (v) only
B) (iii), (iv), and (v) only
C) (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv) only
D) (ii), (iii), and (v) only
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Examine statements (i) and (ii). Statement (i) accurately describes poikilothermy, camouflage (mimicry), hibernation, and aestivation. Statement (ii) accurately lists the external male secondary sexual characters (vocal sacs for croaking and nuptial pads for grasping females during amplexus).
Step 2: Examine statements (iii) and (iv). Frogs respire through skin (cutaneous), buccal cavity (buccopharyngeal), and lungs (pulmonary) as described in (iii). Statement (iv) correctly describes the dual portal systems (hepatic portal and renal portal systems) characteristic of amphibians.
Step 3: Examine statement (v). Statement (v) is false because frogs possess a closed circulatory system with a three-chambered heart (two atria, one ventricle) plus accessory sinus venosus and conus arteriosus.
Step 4: Conclusion. Statements (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv) are correct (Option C).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText:
Match List I with List II regarding sex-specific anatomical and reproductive features in Cockroach (Periplaneta americana) and Frog (Rana tigrina):
List I (Organism & Sex)
A. Male Cockroach
B. Female Cockroach
C. Male Frog
D. Female Frog
List II (Diagnostic Anatomical Trait)
I. Paired unjointed anal styles on $9^{\text{th}}$ abdominal sternite and mushroom-shaped gland in $6^{\text{th}}\text{--}7^{\text{th}}$ segments
II. Boat-shaped $7^{\text{th}}$ sternite forming brood pouch with $8^{\text{th}}$ and $9^{\text{th}}$ sterna; spermathecae in $6^{\text{th}}$ segment
III. Sound-producing vocal sacs, nuptial pads on the first forelimb digit, and Bidder's canal in kidney
IV. Oviducts that open directly and independently into the cloaca without any functional connection to kidneys
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
B) A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III
C) A-I, B-III, C-II, D-IV
D) A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Match A. Male cockroaches possess anal styles on the 9th sternite (absent in females) and mushroom gland in 6th-7th segments. Thus, A matches with I.
Step 2: Match B. Female cockroaches possess a boat-shaped 7th sternite that forms the brood pouch along with 8th and 9th sterna, and a pair of spermathecae in the 6th segment. Thus, B matches with II.
Step 3: Match C. Male frogs possess vocal sacs on the throat, nuptial pads on the first foredigit, and Bidder's canal conveying sperms inside the kidneys. Thus, C matches with III.
Step 4: Match D. Female frogs have convoluted oviducts that open separately into the cloaca, maintaining total anatomical separation between renal (urinary) and genital passages. Thus, D matches with IV. Hence, Option A (A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV) is correct.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.questionText:
Analyze the following statements regarding the comparative histology and cellular matrix of animal tissues:
(i) Simple squamous epithelium consists of a single layer of flattened, scale-like cells with irregular boundaries, facilitating passive diffusion in pulmonary alveoli and Bowman's capsules.
(ii) Dense irregular connective tissue contains interlacing bundles of collagen fibers and fibroblasts oriented in various directions, conferring tensile strength to the dermis of the skin.
(iii) Cartilage cells (chondrocytes) are enclosed within small fluid-filled cavities called lacunae in a solid, pliable matrix rich in chondroitin salts.
(iv) Bone possesses an exceptionally hard, non-pliable matrix impregnated with calcium hydroxyapatite and collagen fibers, organized into Haversian systems around osteocytes.
(v) Blood is a specialized fluid connective tissue where mature erythrocytes actively produce, secrete, and cross-link extracellular collagen and elastin fibers in the plasma.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
options: A) (i), (iii), and (v) only
B) (ii), (iv), and (v) only
C) (i), (ii), and (v) only
D) (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv) only
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate statements (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv). Statement (i) accurately describes simple squamous epithelium and its diffusion boundary role. Statement (ii) accurately describes dense irregular connective tissue in skin dermis. Statement (iii) accurately details cartilage pliable matrix and chondrocytes in lacunae. Statement (iv) accurately describes the non-pliable calcified matrix and osteocytes in Haversian canal systems of compact bone.
Step 2: Evaluate statement (v). Statement (v) is completely false. In blood, the intercellular matrix (plasma) is fluid and does not contain structural fibers secreted by cells; fibers (fibrin) are formed only during blood coagulation from soluble plasma fibrinogen produced by the liver. Mature mammalian RBCs lack nuclei and organelles and do not synthesize fibers.
Step 3: Conclusion. Statements (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv) are correct (Option D).
